title: Imran Khan is still “not out”
gist: Hussain Nadim argues that roughly three years of imprisonment, isolation and health deterioration have not broken former Pakistan PM Imran Khan but made him more symbolically powerful, creating a deadlock for Pakistan's military. A Supreme Court order for private medical treatment was refused by the government, prompting seven former Australian cricket captains and stars like Pat Cummins to appeal for him.

insights.claim: Imran Khan has spent roughly three years in prison after falling foul of Pakistan's powerful military, with much of the past year in prolonged isolation, no public images and a media ban on mentioning his name.
insights.speaker: Hussain Nadim
insights.so_what: Signals entrenched military control and suppressed political competition in Pakistan.

insights.claim: Pressure on Khan has backfired: the more pressure applied to break him, the more powerful the symbolism of his imprisonment, creating a deadlock for a military that historically sidelined leaders via prison or exile.
insights.speaker: Hussain Nadim
insights.so_what: Persistent political instability risk in Pakistan with no clean resolution path.
insights.quote: the more pressure applied to break him, the more powerful the symbolism of his imprisonment becomes

insights.claim: After his removal as PM in a military-backed no-confidence vote, Khan's popularity grew rather than faded, increasing anxiety in Pakistan's centres of power.
insights.speaker: Hussain Nadim
insights.so_what: PTI support remains a latent source of unrest and electoral volatility.
insights.quote: The more pressure brought against him, the more popular he became.

insights.claim: Pakistan's Supreme Court ordered Khan receive treatment at a private hospital, but the government refused, sparking fresh public outrage amid reports of severe eye damage and psychological trauma.
insights.speaker: Hussain Nadim
insights.so_what: Executive defiance of the judiciary indicates weak rule of law, a governance risk.

insights.claim: Khan founded Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf after concluding Pakistani politics was rigged against the poor, making him an enemy of the two dominant dynasties and the military establishment; he survived an assassination attempt in November 2022.
insights.speaker: Hussain Nadim
insights.so_what: Context for the depth of elite opposition to PTI.
